original_test_intent: Validate the GB-NV-PVP tray's built-in simulated-leak function end to end: the correct tray senses the synthetic condition, performs its defined protective turn-off, publishes the correct BMC events, and returns to healthy no-leak operation.
original_method: Pin the GB-NV-PVP tray/controller and firmware, obtain its supported self-test invocation and response table, establish complete management and controller baselines, run one approved simulation, observe the protective state transition and BMC event chain, and prove the documented restoration without introducing coolant.
manual_activity: The GB-NV-PVP owner or FAE approves the platform-specific self-test and recovery; an authorized operator supervises tray behavior and service impact while evidence is captured.
required_inputs: Exact supported self-test utility, command, or BMC action
Leak sensor, controller, valve/pump, and BMC channel correlation
Expected turn-off target, state sequence, events, and deadlines
Secure access plus approved abort, restore, and recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Validate the trigger against the exact GB-NV-PVP firmware
Run only in the approved service window
Never substitute real PG25 or other coolant
Do not expose credentials or clear/filter away management evidence
Abort on physical leak, unexpected actuator state, lost management, or undefined recovery
Preserve all evidence and prohibit automatic repeat
agent_execution_scope: Verify platform/version and receive approved trigger
Record complete tray/BMC baseline and response evidence if authorized
Correlate controller, actuator, sensor, and event timestamps
Do not transpose the generic HW trigger, invent identifiers, manipulate coolant, retry faults, or issue the engineer verdict
engineer_actions: Own the GB-NV-PVP command and compatibility matrix
Define which component turns off and its timing
Approve signal/event identities and service-impact limits
Authorize recovery and determine PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic ipmitool reads can corroborate BMC reporting but cannot select or exercise the GB-NV-PVP tray self-test; grep output may conceal relevant state and inline secrets are prohibited.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Invoke only the version-matched GB-NV-PVP vendor self-test supplied by its owner, surrounded by full secret-safe sensor, controller, Redfish, and SEL collection.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Simulated leak, tray detection, protective turn-off, correct BMC signals, no bundle, and 60/60-minute allocation remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat trigger, tray identity, transient actuator behavior, management events, and final recovery as one time-correlated transaction.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Resolves the otherwise implicit platform interface and evidence acceptance without converting the test to a generic BMC sensor query.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A generic row or adjacent HW implementation cannot establish that this GB-NV-PVP controller path and channel mapping work.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Wrong-platform commands may actuate unexpected tray controls; an incomplete restoration may leave cooling protection or availability degraded.

review_improvement: Makes platform identity and the complete simulated-event lifecycle explicit, preventing adjacent-row substitution, grep-only proof, insecure access, real-coolant use, and automatic retry.
independent_technical_reasoning: The key differentiator is not the shared LC.2 title but the GB-NV-PVP controller implementation. A valid result must show that the command reached this tray instance, that its expected internal sensor state caused the intended actuator transition, and that the same transaction produced correctly mapped BMC events. Capturing the recovery edge matters as much as the assertion edge because a controller can report the test correctly yet remain latched or leave a pump/valve in a service-affecting state. Therefore neither the neighboring generic HW evidence nor a filtered sensor list is substitutable.
